verdict.probe_answer: Both arms implement all 9 trait methods (create_batch, get_batch, list_batches, active_batches, batch_children, claim_batch_child, cancel_batch_if_working, settle_batch_if_status, fail_batch_if_status) with matching SQL/schema/migration. claim_batch_child is genuinely transactional in both: the SELECT-then-INSERT runs synchronously while holding the connection Mutex, wrapped in BEGIN IMMEDIATE, which takes SQLite's write lock before the SELECT — no other claim can interleave, no TOCTOU. Arm A uses rusqlite's built-in Transaction::new_unchecked(&conn, Immediate) (verified this is a safe, non-unsafe fn in rusqlite 0.32.1, the version pinned in this repo's Cargo.lock) with RAII rollback-on-drop. Arm B hand-rolls BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK via raw execute_batch inside a closure with manual rollback on Err — functionally equivalent but less defensive against a mid-transaction panic or failed commit. Arm B hardcodes the inserted status to TaskRecordStatus::Working rather than trusting rec.status (Arm A uses rec.status.as_str()), matching the plan's literal instruction more strictly — a minor robustness edge for B.
verdict.rationale: Production code is nearly identical: same schema, same 9 method bodies, same CAS semantics, same migration placement. The material difference is test coverage. Arm A's migration test also asserts a duplicate-batch-id INSERT errors and exercises the full CAS chain (cancel_batch_if_working, settle_batch_if_status, fail_batch_if_status, active_batches transitions in/out), and its claim test additionally verifies the ExistingTerminal branch by settling a child terminal and reclaiming. Arm B's versions of both named tests are stripped to the bare minimum and never exercise cancel/settle/fail/active_batches/list_batches at all — 5 of 9 methods ship with zero automated coverage. Given the task's explicit TDD instruction and that CAS/claim logic is the concurrency-sensitive core of this feature, that gap is a real reviewable deficiency a reviewer would flag before merge, not style. Arm B's minor edge (hardcoding inserted status) doesn't offset this gap.
